summary:
[TO WILLIAM B. WOLFSON1  


I may be unable to travel to San Rafael for my court appearance because of financial problems, as we discussed on the phone. Of course I will make every effort to be there, but in the meantime this statement of my present general situa­ tion may be of use to you. 

I have debts amounting to several thousands of dollars. Since my wife Nancy left me, taking our daughter, I have not been able to complete a single piece of writing, either a story or a novel, except for a speech I wrote for the Vancouver Science Fiction Convention in February, 1972. It took me four years to write the speech. At the time Nancy left (I believe August 1970) I was in the midst of working on a novel; it remains unfinished to this day, over two years later. All my income, which has been steadily dwindling, has come from residual royalties from previous work, such as foreign editions; therefore I have made less and less money each month until now I am deep in debt including a debt to my own agent in my field, through whom my royalties come. Liter­ ally, I am now living on money borrowed from him against supposed future royalties. I am behind in my gas and electric bills, by over two months. I have raised the rent money which was due on my apartment the first of this month, but haven’t paid it because if I do I won’t have money for food.
